$comment: Who answers for each robot account (non-human identity) in the lab tenant, and why (ADR 0018 and its 2026-11-05 amendments; nhi-standard N1). 06-NHI-Inventory.ps1 -OwnersRegisterPath reads it.
An Entra owner can add a credential to the app and act AS it, so ownership is power, not a label. Two owner models:
ownerModel 'entra' - two named admin (adm-) accounts own the app in Entra, the inventory checks them (OWNER-NONE / OWNER-NO-HUMAN / OWNER-SINGLE). Never a workforce account, never break-glass.

ownerModel 'role'  - a Tier-0 identity: NO Entra owner at all, because a standing owner would hold Tier-0 power outside PIM (ADR 0020 zero standing access). Its accountable owner is a ROLE below; changes go only through reviewed code (envs/bootstrap, envs/operator), whose Terraform sets owners to an empty list. The inventory counts it as owned while it has no Entra owner and flags any Entra owner (OWNER-TIER0).
SOD-08 (lab/iga/sod-rules.json): the access governance lead certifies access, so she never owns an identity that creates, changes or disables accounts.

Where each Entra list lives: modules/apps apps = envs/dev secret TF_APP_OWNER_OBJECT_IDS; the HR provisioning app = envs/bootstrap hr_provisioning_owner_object_ids (one owner resource per person, registration only); P2P Server and the Cloud Sync app = the post-apply step below. Object ids are not kept here: resolve an admin account with GET /users/<upn>?$select=id.

Identity Platform Owner.holder: the identity platform owner - in the lab, the repository maintainer (risk owner in ADR 0005 and ADR 0024)
Identity Platform Owner.answersFor: each Tier-0 identity's purpose, permissions and credentials, the quarterly Tier-0 permission review (nhi-standard section 4) and the kill switch; changes only through reviewed pull requests, never by owning the app in Entra

people.adm-mei.tanaka: Mei Tanaka, access governance lead (certifies access: SOD-08 side B)
people.adm-ava.lin: Ava Lin, IAM engineer (Tier-0 eligible through PIM)
people.adm-raj.patel: Raj Patel, service desk analyst (PIM-Tier1-Helpdesk; SOD-08 side A only - certifies nothing, reviews nothing, manages no one holding requested access)

identities.why: Reads the envs/dev Terraform state, which holds the generated break-glass passwords (envs/bootstrap main.tf, 'Remote state').
Writes the audit evidence into the WORM store; an owner who could act as it could add evidence nobody can remove.
Its uploads create and disable workforce accounts, executives included.
Staff sign-in and SCIM accounts in AWS; no Graph permission.
Staff sign-in to the IT help desk; no Graph permission.
Creates and switches off ServiceNow accounts from App-ServiceNow-Users; no Graph permission.
The clinical portal's sign-in and app roles; no Graph application permission.
Entra as the identity provider for the acquired clinic's Okta; delegated sign-in scopes only.
Made by Entra device registration when vm-win11-01 joined (2026-10-29); no permission, no credential.

identities.managedBy: envs/bootstrap hr_provisioning_owner_object_ids (registration only; HR-SYNC stays an owner for .OwnedBy)
identities.why: Its job creates and disables AD accounts: not the access governance lead (SOD-08). The registration has no Graph permission and no credential; the job on its service principal stays out of the help desk's hands.

identities.managedBy: post-apply (adm-ava.lin: registration + service principal; adm-raj.patel: registration only)
identities.why: Cloud Sync's configuration app (AD to Entra). Not the access governance lead (SOD-08). The registration has no permission and no credential; the sync job on its service principal is owned by the IAM engineer only, so the help desk gets no say over what Cloud Sync writes (the restricted VIP unit stays out of its reach).

outOfScope.what: Managed identities: vm-win11-01, vm-dc01, id-kv-idlab-reader, pb-identity-contain, pb-identity-notify
outOfScope.why: Entra has no owners for a managed identity; it lives and dies with its Azure resource, and who controls it is Azure RBAC on that resource (the inventory's OwnerModel 'Azure RBAC on the resource').

outOfScope.what: Vendor apps: Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools, O365 LinkedIn Connection
outOfScope.why: Multi-tenant apps registered in Microsoft's own tenants (publisher Microsoft): their owners are the publisher. This tenant governs them through consent (ADR 0018 consent policy), not ownership.
Owned and run by Microsoft; the inventory counts them and leaves them out.

postApplyStep.add: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications/{app object id}/owners/$ref (and /servicePrincipals/{sp object id}/owners/$ref where the row says so), body {"@odata.id": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/directoryObjects/{admin account object id}"}
postApplyStep.docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/application-post-owners and .../serviceprincipal-post-owners: app-only needs Application.ReadWrite.All + Directory.Read.All (Learn: Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy is not sufficient to add another owner)
